source: Actual local k3d native RBAC operations and signed AWS SDK for Go v2 reads against a race-instrumented stackd executable; not a native AWS GuardDuty capture
corrections: The first native binding workflow passed native creations, negative controls and restart, then its SDK helper incorrectly compared all detector findings with only the EKS expectations. The corrected helper uses the modeled resource.resourceType=EKSCluster filter and still requires the exact native finding set.

A generated-name decoder regression failed before the fix. The decoder now derives an absent objectRef.name from the actual admitted response; it still rejects mismatches. The corrected native workflow also exercises generateName.
verification: Memory/SQLite source rollback, replay, isolation, mutable-reader detachment and restart regressions passed under go test -race ./internal/integrations -run TestGuardDutyKubernetesSourceTransactionAndDurableAdmission -count=1.
Affected package and SDK helper vet/staticcheck passed.
The full native workflow ran against a race-instrumented executable and exited successfully.
Complete finding catalog generation and deterministic check passed.
limits: Anonymous binding detection requires actual successful non-dry-run create responses; it does not establish general RBAC privilege analysis or evaluate referenced-role policy contents.
Only native RBAC creates use RequestResponse audit level. Other resources remain Metadata; the security journal retains roleRef and subjects, not arbitrary object bodies.
The full 204-type catalog remains the target. Declaration counts do not prove AWS behavior or private-model equivalence.
All exact-owned cloud/runtime resources and successful-run temporary state were cleaned up; this JSON retains the observations.
scope: Actual local EKS/k3d audit operations; no sample findings or injected webhook events
